title: 第15章 正式指导第16章 剑骨印记发烫
content_zh:
天还没亮，顾渊就醒了。
他睁开眼睛，茅草屋的屋顶在视线中慢慢从模糊变得清晰。
胸口还在微微发热——那是昨晚剑骨印记留下的余温，像是被一块温热的石头贴了一整夜。
顾渊坐起来，没有立刻动弹。
他低头看着自己的双手——掌心纹路清晰，老茧粗糙，手指因为常年握剑而有些变形。
昨晚的一切像是一场梦，但那余温告诉他，那不是梦。
剑里有一个人。
一个在剑中世界等待他的人。
一个愿意教他真正剑道的人。
顾渊系好草鞋，从床底摸出铁剑，推门走了出去。
冬夜即将过去，天边泛起了一抹淡淡的鱼肚白，像是一把被晨曦磨钝的刀，在灰蓝色的天幕上划出一道苍白的痕迹。
空气清冽而干燥，吸进肺里带着一丝寒意，但已经没有前几天那么刺骨了。
顾渊走到后院，没有立刻挥剑。
他在演武场中央站定，握着手中的铁剑，闭上眼睛。
他在等。
等那个声音。
一分钟。
两分钟。
三分钟。
什么都没有发生。

剑柄冰冷而沉默，剑身黯淡而安静。
残魂没有说话，光芒没有渗出，意识没有触碰。
顾渊没有急躁。
他只是静静地站着，握着剑，像是在等待一扇门自己打开。
五分钟。
十分钟。
然后，他感觉到了。
从剑柄传来的一丝极其微弱的震颤，像是某种沉睡的东西翻了个身。
那震颤很短暂，几乎难以察觉，但顾渊确确实实地感觉到了——他的掌心与剑柄贴合了四年，剑的每一分变化他都了如指掌。
“太早了。“残魂的声音在意识中响起，低沉而沙哑，带着一种刚睡醒的模糊感。
“天还没亮。“
顾渊在意识中回答：“你说今天开始。“
“我说的是天亮以后。“
“天亮以后就是明天。“
“我睡不着。“
残魂沉默了一瞬。
然后，顾渊感觉到剑身内部的某种东西动了一下——不是肉体的动弹，而是某种意识的舒展，像是一个人从床上坐起来，伸了个懒腰。
“你这种性格——“残魂的声音里带着一丝若有若无的无奈。
“在古代，叫做'执念太深'。“
“现在呢？“

“现在叫'疯子'。“
顾渊没有接话。
他只是握着剑，安静地等待。
残魂又沉默了一会儿。
content_en:
Gu Yuan woke up before dawn.
He opened his eyes, and the roof of the thatched house slowly became clear in his sight.
His chest was still slightly warm - it was the residual warmth left by the sword bone mark last night, as if a warm stone had been pressed against it all night.
Gu Yuan sat up and did not move immediately.
He looked down at his hands - the palms had clear lines and rough calluses, and the fingers were somewhat deformed from holding swords for many years.
Everything last night seemed like a dream, but the residual warmth told him that it was not a dream.
There is a man in the sword.
A man waiting for him in the world of swords.
Someone who was willing to teach him the true way of the sword.
Gu Yuan tied up his straw sandals, took out the iron sword from under the bed, opened the door and walked out.
The winter night is about to pass, and a faint fish belly white appears on the horizon, like a knife blunted by the morning sun, drawing a pale trace on the gray-blue sky.
The air was crisp and dry, bringing a chill to the lungs, but it was no longer as biting as the previous few days.
Gu Yuan walked to the backyard and did not wave his sword immediately.
He stood still in the center of the martial arts arena, holding the iron sword in his hand and closing his eyes.
He is waiting.
Wait for that voice.
One minute.
Two minutes.
Three minutes.
Nothing happened.
The hilt is cold and silent, and the sword body is dim and quiet.
The remnant soul did not speak, the light did not seep out, and the consciousness did not touch.
Gu Yuan was not impatient.
He just stood quietly, holding the sword, as if waiting for a door to open by itself.
Five minutes.
Ten minutes.
Then he felt it.
An extremely weak tremor came from the hilt of the sword, like something sleeping turning over.
The tremor was short and almost imperceptible, but Gu Yuan definitely felt it - his palm had been in contact with the hilt of the sword for four years, and he was aware of every change of the sword.
"It's too early." Remnant Soul's voice sounded in his consciousness, low and hoarse, with a vague feeling of just waking up from sleep.
"It's still dark."
Gu Yuan answered in his mind: "You said we would start today."
"I'm talking about after dawn."
"After dawn, there will be tomorrow."
"I can't sleep."
Remnant Soul was silent for a moment.
Then, Gu Yuan felt something inside the sword move - not a physical movement, but some kind of stretching of consciousness, like a person sitting up from bed and stretching.
"You have this kind of character -" There was a hint of helplessness in Canhun's voice.
"In ancient times, it was called 'too deep of an obsession'."
"What now?"
"Now called 'Crazy'."
Gu Yuan didn't answer.
He just held the sword and waited quietly.
Remnant Soul was silent for a while.
